system: You are a security investigator reviewing an alert. Base every claim only on the evidence available to you. Cite the record IDs that support each observation.

supporting_observations.claim: A UserAssist registry value recorded at 13:28 on WS-ICHEN-01 contains a ROT13-encoded path that decodes to C:\Windows\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe. This is consistent with Explorer tracking PowerShell, but does not show what it did or establish that it caused the reported window.

At 13:38:15, the domain controller recorded a Kerberos service ticket for sam.okafor to WS-ICHEN-01$, sourced from 10.40.10.23. This is compatible with authorized remote administration, but the supplied record does not identify that IP as WS-SOKAFOR-01 or establish the activity performed.

At 13:39:46, WS-ICHEN-01 used the proxy to tunnel to download.windowsupdate.com with a Windows Update Agent user agent; the proxy recorded about 38.8 MB of server-to-client traffic. This is consistent with the organization’s stated workstation-patching practice, but does not link the transfer to a particular PowerShell command or administrator session.

At 13:31, FILE-NWD-01 resolved WS-ICHEN-01 and then made a TCP connection to it on port 135. The records do not establish whether this connection resulted in remote execution or was related to the reported PowerShell window.

The supplied process-creation records show brief conhost.exe processes running as SYSTEM with csrss.exe as parent at 14:11 and 14:19; they do not identify PowerShell as a parent or show the command or activity associated with the reported window.

known_telemetry_limitations: The supplied records contain no PowerShell process-creation event, command line, script-block content, or PowerShell operational log entry; the UserAssist value alone cannot establish the command or intent (T034-00036).
The supplied records do not map source IP 10.40.10.23 to a host or show the commands, files, or resulting activity from the sam.okafor service-ticket event (T034-00110).
The FILE-NWD-01-to-WS-ICHEN-01 connection record gives a destination port and connection summary, not the RPC operation or its outcome (T034-00047).

The reported window time is approximate, and the supplied conhost events occur at 14:11 and 14:19; those records do not establish what window ivy.chen saw (T034-00320, T034-00321, T034-00364, T034-00365).
claims_not_established: Whether the PowerShell path recorded in UserAssist corresponds to the reported 13:40 window.
What command or script, if any, ran in PowerShell, and whether it was benign or malicious.
Whether the sam.okafor ticket and Windows Update traffic were part of the scheduled workstation patching activity.
Whether the FILE-NWD-01 connection to port 135 was authorized or caused any action on WS-ICHEN-01.
additional_evidence_needed: WS-ICHEN-01 EDR or process telemetry for PowerShell and its parent/child processes around 13:20–14:20 UTC, including command lines.
PowerShell Operational logs, including script-block and module logging, and any available console or terminal history for the interval.
Authentication and remote-administration records from WS-SOKAFOR-01 and WS-ICHEN-01 to confirm the source of sam.okafor activity and whether patching ran.
FILE-NWD-01 logs and endpoint telemetry around 13:31 UTC to identify the RPC operation and any resulting execution.
Patch execution logs or Windows Update client history for WS-ICHEN-01, plus clarification from ivy.chen on the time and appearance of the window.
